title: Digital Experience Reference Library
method: Primary creator, brand and product sources. Design interpretations are hypotheses, not measured engagement claims. Only Absurd Trolley Problems was interacted with during this research pass; other pages and case studies were researched, not end-to-end playtested. Historical campaign availability is not inferred from a surviving case study.

references.name: Draw a Perfect Circle
references.creator: Neal Agarwal
references.action: Draw a circle around the marker and receive a percentage score.
references.appeal: The task sounds easy; the visible gap between intention and result invites another attempt.
references.borrow: One sentence, one gesture, one legible result.
references.dependency: A fair scoring rule and responsive drawing matter more than adding a themed background.

references.name: Absurd Trolley Problems
references.creator: Neal Agarwal
references.action: Choose whether to divert a trolley, then see how other participants answered.
references.appeal: Difficult or absurd scenarios create tension; comparison adds a second payoff.
references.borrow: Make the choice itself interesting before adding animation or personalization.
references.dependency: Requires strong scenario writing and honest aggregate results. Two buttons are not inherently a weak experience.

references.name: Spend Bill Gates’ Money
references.creator: Neal Agarwal
references.action: Allocate an enormous imaginary budget across a catalog of things to buy and sell.
references.appeal: An impossible fantasy becomes a concrete series of personal decisions.
references.borrow: Give people a vivid constraint and let them express priorities through familiar objects.
references.dependency: The catalog and price contrasts do the creative work. A random shopping list would lose the premise.

references.name: Space Elevator
references.creator: Neal Agarwal
references.action: Scroll upward through an illustrated journey with altitude milestones and facts.
references.appeal: Physical distance supplies a natural progress indicator; each height promises another discovery.
references.borrow: Make navigation correspond to the subject instead of decorating an ordinary scroll page.
references.dependency: Needs a researched sequence and authored illustrations; length alone does not create curiosity.

references.name: XOX
references.creator: makemepulse
references.action: Play a familiar tic-tac-toe game presented with crafted motion and responsive visuals.
references.appeal: Familiar rules leave attention available for the feel and personality of the interaction.
references.borrow: Keep the rules recognizable; invest in response timing, transitions and character.
references.dependency: The creator documents the design, not an independently measured retention lift.

references.name: GeoGuessr
references.creator: GeoGuessr
references.action: Inspect street imagery for clues and guess the location on a map.
references.appeal: Inference turns ordinary environmental details into useful evidence.
references.borrow: A guessing game becomes compelling when people can reason from real clues.
references.dependency: Depends on geographic imagery, location data and game services; account or payment requirements may apply.

references.name: Gridland
references.creator: doublespeak games
references.action: Match tiles to build a settlement by day and respond to threats at night.
references.appeal: A familiar interaction changes meaning when the world shifts between two states.
references.borrow: Introduce one understandable action, then change its consequences.
references.dependency: Requires balanced resource and combat systems; a full game is a larger commitment than a campaign page.

references.name: A Dark Room
references.creator: doublespeak games
references.action: Begin with lighting a fire; further actions and a larger world gradually become available.
references.appeal: The small opening creates a question about what will emerge next.
references.borrow: Reveal complexity after participation instead of explaining the entire concept upfront.
references.dependency: Progression needs authored discoveries and balanced pacing; hiding weak content is not mystery.

references.name: Patatap
references.creator: Jono Brandel / Lullatone
references.action: Use taps or keys to trigger paired sounds and animated shapes.
references.appeal: An ordinary gesture produces a surprisingly expressive audiovisual response.
references.borrow: Make the first touch satisfying without instructions or a score.
references.dependency: Needs a coherent sound and animation palette. Flashing visuals also affect who can comfortably use it.

references.name: Blob Opera
references.creator: David Li / Google Arts & Culture
references.action: Drag singing characters to control pitch and vowel sounds while other voices harmonize.
references.appeal: People can produce a convincing musical performance with very little musical knowledge.
references.borrow: Constrain the system so experimentation tends to sound good.
references.dependency: The musical model and expressive animation are core capabilities, not decorative details.

references.name: Song Maker
references.creator: Google Creative Lab
references.action: Make and share a song using a browser music-making tool.
references.appeal: Actions accumulate into something the visitor can hear and claim as their own.
references.borrow: Deliver a real creation, with a short path from editing to playback.
references.dependency: Needs usable composition controls, playback and a meaningful sharing format.

references.name: Quick, Draw!
references.creator: Google
references.action: Draw a requested object within a short time limit while a model tries to recognize it.
references.appeal: The machine’s guesses turn drawing into a responsive back-and-forth.
references.borrow: Expose intermediate feedback so the system feels present during the action.
references.dependency: Recognition quality and failure behavior shape the fun; a static result cannot substitute for the loop.

references.name: AutoDraw
references.creator: Google Creative Lab
references.action: Sketch a shape and choose a suggested polished drawing.
references.appeal: A rough attempt quickly becomes something useful and presentable.
references.borrow: Help visitors succeed at a task they might otherwise avoid.
references.dependency: The suggestion model and curated artwork make the transformation credible.

references.name: Silk
references.creator: Yuri Vishnevsky
references.action: Draw flowing patterns with color, symmetry and mirroring controls, then save the image.
references.appeal: Small gestures generate elaborate compositions without requiring drawing skill.
references.borrow: Make the output feel authored by the visitor while the system supplies visual coherence.
references.dependency: Good defaults and tuned rendering are essential; arbitrary particle effects are not enough.

references.name: Sandspiel
references.creator: Max Bittker
references.action: Paint materials into a simulated world, observe their interactions and share creations.
references.appeal: Simple rules combine into surprising outcomes and self-directed experiments.
references.borrow: Use a small vocabulary of behaviors that interact meaningfully.
references.dependency: The simulation needs consistent rules and performance headroom; community sharing adds storage and moderation.

references.name: Incredibox
references.creator: So Far So Good
references.action: Assign sounds to animated performers, combine parts and record or share a mix.
references.appeal: Mixing becomes a performance; particular combinations reveal additional rewards.
references.borrow: Pair modular content with characters and a coherent musical palette.
references.dependency: Requires authored compatible audio loops, animation and timing; song analysis alone does not provide those assets.

references.name: Townscaper
references.creator: Oskar Stålberg / Raw Fury
references.action: Place colored blocks that automatically form houses, bridges and other town structures.
references.appeal: The system turns modest inputs into an attractive place, without demanding a win condition.
references.borrow: Automate the hard craft while preserving meaningful creative control.
references.dependency: Procedural architecture is the product; this is not a generic 3D scene with a build button.

references.name: Create a Minifigure
references.creator: LEGO
references.action: Combine heads, bodies, legs and accessories into a LEGO character.
references.appeal: Familiar parts let people make recognizable versions of themselves or someone they know.
references.borrow: Use a constrained asset kit that supports distinct identities.
references.dependency: The options must be expressive and compatible; commerce adds stock and fulfillment requirements.

references.name: LOOPY
references.creator: Nicky Case
references.action: Draw a system of connected elements, run it and explore changes.
references.appeal: A diagram becomes something that responds to questions rather than a fixed explanation.
references.borrow: Let people manipulate the relationship the experience is trying to explain.
references.dependency: A model is an authored simplification, not proof of how a real system behaves.

references.name: Gartic Phone
references.creator: Onrizon
references.action: Alternate writing descriptions and drawing other people’s prompts, then reveal the chain.
references.appeal: Misinterpretations become a shared punchline that no single participant could author alone.
references.borrow: Design a reveal that makes everyone’s contribution matter.
references.dependency: Needs enough participants, coordination and suitable prompts; an empty room has no payoff.

references.name: skribbl.io
references.creator: skribbl.io
references.action: Take turns drawing while others guess the word and earn points.
references.appeal: A familiar social game creates immediate roles, uncertainty and friendly competition.
references.borrow: Give spectators an active job while another person performs.
references.dependency: Multiplayer availability, moderation and synchronized rounds are fundamental requirements.

references.name: Mon Top Netflix
references.creator: Netflix / makemepulse
references.action: Choose and rank favorite Netflix shows, then produce a personal top-ten social asset.
references.appeal: People already have opinions about the catalog; arranging them becomes an identity statement.
references.borrow: Ask for a real opinion and give it a polished, recognizable form.
references.dependency: Needs a catalog people care about and strong export design; arbitrary preferences are weaker.

references.name: Ciao Bella — Nairobi tribute
references.creator: Netflix / makemepulse
references.action: Contribute artwork, images, videos or letters to a tribute for a La Casa de Papel character.
references.appeal: Participation expresses an existing emotional attachment and makes other fans visible.
references.borrow: Give a community a specific occasion and a meaningful contribution format.
references.dependency: Requires moderation and an authentic shared attachment; a generic guestbook will not create either.

references.name: Spotify Wrapped 2025
references.creator: Spotify
references.action: Explore a personalized account of the year’s listening and share selected results.
references.appeal: Real history produces recognition, surprise and comparison with friends.
references.borrow: Turn authentic behavior into an editorially designed personal story.
references.dependency: Requires sufficient first-party listening history; a few quiz answers cannot imply the same evidential depth.

references.name: Strava Year in Sport 2023
references.creator: Strava / Hello Monday
references.action: Revisit activity statistics and personal achievements through a designed annual recap.
references.appeal: The result gives form to effort the person actually invested.
references.borrow: Celebrate earned progress with a narrative and memorable visual language.
references.dependency: Needs accurate activity data and thoughtful selection; generic praise has little meaning.

references.name: See Yourself in Sound
references.creator: Bang & Olufsen / Hello Monday
references.action: Use listening information or an emoji questionnaire to generate a character and a shareable animated expression of musical taste.
references.appeal: The output is a distinctive little performance rather than a label attached to a questionnaire.
references.borrow: Invest in the desirability of the result, not only the questions leading to it.
references.dependency: Depends on a curated character, motion and audio system; the questionnaire path is interpretation, not verified listening history.

references.name: Nike App GTM
references.creator: Nike / UNIT9
references.action: Turn existing Nike activity and purchase information into a personalized animated journey.
references.appeal: Recognizable history makes the branded presentation about the participant.
references.borrow: Use information already meaningful to the person to shape the narrative.
references.dependency: Requires account integrations, data access and authored animation; a visual clone cannot supply the personal substance.

references.name: Nike Wall of Dreams
references.creator: Nike / UNIT9
references.action: Create a personalized football-star poster using a photo and customized text.
references.appeal: The visitor can see themselves inside an aspirational visual world.
references.borrow: Make a keepsake someone would want independently of the campaign call to action.
references.dependency: Portrait handling and high-quality composition are central; a name pasted on a generic card is a weaker result.

references.name: Gucci Town
references.creator: Gucci / Roblox
references.action: Visit branded spaces, play minigames, create and collect virtual items in Roblox.
references.appeal: A recurring social setting gives people several ways to participate and express affiliation.
references.borrow: Build related activities around a coherent world and useful identity objects.
references.dependency: Depends on a platform community, ongoing content and virtual goods; not a one-off standalone browser site.

references.name: Crackables 2.0
references.creator: OnePlus / UNIT9
references.action: Solve cryptographic puzzles through a staged competition with community participation and a finale.
references.appeal: Mystery and shared progress give people reasons to discuss the experience outside the site.
references.borrow: Create clues that reward thinking and collaboration rather than arbitrary clicking.
references.dependency: Puzzle design, event operations, competition rules and rewards carry substantial work.

references.name: The Xbox Vault
references.creator: Xbox / Netflix / makemepulse
references.action: Explore game-related artifacts in a vault and answer questions under a time limit.
references.appeal: Recognizable objects let fans use knowledge they are proud to possess.
references.borrow: Tie challenges to specific artifacts and memories rather than generic trivia.
references.dependency: Needs licensed assets, credible questions and accessible navigation; historical campaign availability is unverified.

references.name: NARS Play Your Power
references.creator: NARS / makemepulse
references.action: Play a motorcycle runner through a stylized world with lipstick-shade characters and powers.
references.appeal: Product identity becomes a visible game world and selectable character.
references.borrow: Translate brand attributes into art, movement and meaningful options.
references.dependency: Needs real runner mechanics, balanced powers and a coherent asset set; packaging alone will not make play rewarding.

references.name: Nike Sport Wonderland
references.creator: Nike / UNIT9
references.action: Explore a campaign map containing different movement, expression and relaxation activities.
references.appeal: Variety offers multiple entry points while a shared world connects the activities.
references.borrow: Use a collection when each activity has a clear, different appeal.
references.dependency: The documented campaign used platform integration and time-based operations; camera games need alternatives.

references.name: Nike Reactland
references.creator: Nike / UNIT9
references.action: Run on a treadmill to control a personalized character in a digital environment.
references.appeal: Trying the product becomes the control scheme rather than an interruption before a game.
references.borrow: Let the product’s actual use produce the interaction.
references.dependency: Requires an installation, sensing and staff; study the connection, not as a browser-ready template.

references.name: Orange Cube Engage
references.creator: Orange / makemepulse
references.action: Join team challenges across a collection of games over a multiweek employee event.
references.appeal: Team identity and scheduled variety create reasons to return together.
references.borrow: An ongoing experience needs social structure and a content calendar.
references.dependency: Participation is supported by an organization and campaign operations; do not attribute it solely to UI.

references.name: Intuit Salescraft
references.creator: Intuit / makemepulse
references.action: Complete learning activities that contribute to an evolving game world and team construction.
references.appeal: Visible shared progress connects individual effort to a larger outcome.
references.borrow: Show consequences of participation that persist beyond a badge.
references.dependency: Needs learning integration, sustained content and fair progress rules; adding a city skin does not improve lessons.

references.name: 30 Years of NARS
references.creator: NARS / makemepulse
references.action: Explore an editorial celebration of the brand through themed visual chapters.
references.appeal: Strong archival material and changing compositions can sustain exploration without a score.
references.borrow: Let valuable content and art direction carry a quieter experience.
references.dependency: Requires an interesting archive, editorial selection and strong media; elaborate navigation cannot replace them.

references.name: LEGO Brick Lab
references.creator: LEGO
references.action: Build a physical creation and see it incorporated into a digital experience.
references.appeal: The object made by the visitor becomes part of a larger world.
references.borrow: Make the contribution recognizable after transformation.
references.dependency: The documented experience depends on scanning, an installation and venue operations.

references.name: MoMA Magritte
references.creator: MoMA / Hello Monday
references.action: Explore a painter’s work through narrative, sound and interactive views of conservation imagery.
references.appeal: Revealing hidden layers gives interaction a purpose tied directly to the art.
references.borrow: Use interaction to reveal something visitors could not see in an ordinary image.
references.dependency: Needs compelling source material and editorial pacing; special effects alone cannot supply discovery.

references.name: Into the Arctic
references.creator: Greenpeace / Hello Monday
references.action: Follow an expedition through an evolving digital logbook with wildlife and environmental context.
references.appeal: Real events and new entries give a reason to revisit a continuing story.
references.borrow: Use genuine developments as the return loop instead of manufacturing daily chores.
references.dependency: Requires fresh reporting and an editorial schedule; historical case study, not a current expedition tracker.

references.name: Bear 71
references.creator: National Film Board of Canada
references.action: Experience a wildlife documentary through a bear’s narrated perspective and an interactive surveillance landscape.
references.appeal: The interface reinforces the story’s perspective and questions about observation.
references.borrow: Make the method of exploration part of what the story means.
references.dependency: Requires authored documentary media and careful navigation; legacy or VR versions may have compatibility limits.

references.name: The Boat
references.creator: SBS / Matt Huynh
references.action: Move through a graphic adaptation combining illustrated scenes, text, motion and sound.
references.appeal: Pacing and sensory treatment support immersion in a specific narrative.
references.borrow: Compose transitions around story beats instead of adding decorative scroll effects.
references.dependency: Needs excellent writing, illustration and sound direction; the source describes a historical release.

references.name: NASA Eyes
references.creator: NASA
references.action: Explore missions, planets and spacecraft through interactive 3D views based on NASA information.
references.appeal: Scale and otherwise inaccessible places become navigable and comparable.
references.borrow: Give people meaningful destinations and controls for a subject they are curious about.
references.dependency: Requires authoritative data, 3D assets and accurate explanatory context.

references.name: Radio Garden
references.creator: Radio Garden
references.action: Explore live radio stations around the world through a geographic interface.
references.appeal: Every destination provides immediate, authentic sound from another place.
references.borrow: Make browsing itself deliver the content instead of leading through layers of menus.
references.dependency: Depends on station streams and geographic data; availability varies by stream and location.

references.name: Zoomquilt
references.creator: Zoomquilt collaborators
references.action: Watch an illustrated world continuously zoom into further scenes.
references.appeal: The next image grows out of the current one, sustaining anticipation.
references.borrow: Design continuity between scenes so the transition itself is the attraction.
references.dependency: This is largely a viewing experience, not evidence that every site needs active controls.

references.name: Dicing an Onion
references.creator: The Pudding
references.action: Adjust cutting parameters and inspect how the simulated pieces change.
references.appeal: A familiar practical question becomes something people can test for themselves.
references.borrow: Connect every control to a visible consequence and a specific question.
references.dependency: Requires a sound explanatory model; impressive controls cannot compensate for a wrong model.

references.name: NYC’s Urban Textscape
references.creator: The Pudding
references.action: Search visible words captured on New York City streets.
references.appeal: A familiar city becomes a surprising searchable collection of details.
references.borrow: Reveal a new way to explore existing material rather than inventing unrelated lore.
references.dependency: Depends on a prepared image and text dataset. Interaction description is supported by the publisher index; dynamic page text was limited.

references.name: Look at the Sky
references.creator: Porter Robinson / Active Theory
references.action: Listen in a shared visual environment that changes with the song and allows expressive trails.
references.appeal: The song supplies the experience’s pacing and emotional world.
references.borrow: Let the original work be the center of participation.
references.dependency: Synchronized playback, timed media and shared presence require capabilities beyond a static page.

references.name: Almost Forgot
references.creator: J.Views / Hello Monday
references.action: Use a finger on the phone camera to influence a music experience through detected pulse.
references.appeal: A bodily signal becomes a direct connection to the music.
references.borrow: Use an input whose relationship to the experience is understandable.
references.dependency: Needs camera access, robust signal detection and adaptable playback; an alternate path is important.

references.name: Headbanger.ai
references.creator: Hello Monday
references.action: Control a breakout-style game with tracked head movements while music plays.
references.appeal: A familiar game receives a physical, performative control scheme.
references.borrow: Change one meaningful aspect of a known game instead of inventing confusing new rules.
references.dependency: Tracking quality, camera setup and accessible alternatives determine whether it feels playful or frustrating.

references.name: Signs
references.creator: Hello Monday
references.action: Practice sign language with interactive instruction and feedback, with a contribution path for examples.
references.appeal: Participation produces a usable skill rather than only a score.
references.borrow: Make feedback specific enough to help the person improve.
references.dependency: Requires language expertise and recognition quality; visual polish is not evidence of teaching accuracy.

references.name: Click Click Click
references.creator: Moniker / VPRO
references.action: Move and click in a sparse page while a narrator comments on browser behavior.
references.appeal: The page notices mundane actions and turns them into an unexpected social encounter.
references.borrow: Make the response observant and well written; a simple input can support a rich personality.
references.dependency: The authored voice and timing carry the concept. Profiling is the artwork’s subject, not a recommendation to infer sensitive traits.

references.name: Puff Up Club
references.creator: Moniker / Random
references.action: Work with other online visitors to inflate a real balloon shown through a live stream.
references.appeal: A visible physical consequence builds shared anticipation toward an uncertain moment.
references.borrow: Give collective action a concrete, observable consequence.
references.dependency: Requires hardware, a live feed and operations; the historical installation is not assumed to remain active.

references.name: Your Line or Mine
references.creator: Moniker / Stedelijk Museum
references.action: Follow a short drawing instruction, scan the result and see it become a frame in a collective animation.
references.appeal: A modest personal contribution becomes part of a work larger than any individual drawing.
references.borrow: Constrain contributions enough that they assemble into a coherent result.
references.dependency: Needs a contribution pipeline, composition rules and moderation; originally a museum installation.

references.name: Do Not Touch
references.creator: Light Light / Moniker
references.action: Follow prompts with the pointer during a music video alongside traces of previous participants.
references.appeal: The crowd becomes part of the visual performance and reveals conformity or playful disobedience.
references.borrow: Make participation visibly alter the work, even when people join at different times.
references.dependency: Needs recorded input, video timing and an update pipeline; not simply a live cursor overlay.

references.name: Touch for Luck
references.creator: M+ / Moniker
references.action: Maintain contact with the screen to develop a fish in a shared pond shown on a museum facade.
references.appeal: Accumulating adornments and public presence create attachment to a small personal character.
references.borrow: Study visible persistence and shared presence, while questioning the demand for prolonged attention.
references.dependency: The artwork critiques compulsive engagement; its long hold mechanic is a counterexample to treating time spent as user value.

references.name: Dance Tonite
references.creator: LCD Soundsystem / Moniker / Studio Puckey / Google
references.action: Contribute a recorded dance with room-scale VR or view the collective performance from another device.
references.appeal: Simple shapes retain the personality of real human movement.
references.borrow: Preserve the expressive traces of people rather than replacing them with generic avatars.
references.dependency: Creation required specific VR hardware; viewing and performing were intentionally different roles. Legacy compatibility is unverified.

references.name: The Evolution of Trust
references.creator: Nicky Case
references.action: Explore an interactive explanation of cooperation and trust through game-theory scenarios.
references.appeal: Participation makes an abstract argument something the visitor can examine.
references.borrow: Let an explanation respond to decisions instead of asking people only to read conclusions.
references.dependency: The model is deliberately simplified; do not present its outcomes as universal rules about people.

references.name: How To Remember Anything Forever-ish
references.creator: Nicky Case
references.action: Read an interactive explanation of memory and practice with recall and spaced repetition.
references.appeal: The reader experiences the method while learning why it is used.
references.borrow: Make the experience demonstrate its own idea through participation.
references.dependency: Learning claims need appropriate evidence; the design reference is the integration of explanation and practice.

references.name: We Become What We Behold
references.creator: Nicky Case
references.action: Play a short game about news and self-reinforcing social cycles.
references.appeal: A compact interactive work can communicate a point through consequences.
references.borrow: Use a bounded experience with a deliberate ending when the idea benefits from closure.
references.dependency: The satirical theme and escalating consequences require authored content; it is not a universal template for cheerful campaigns.
